title: Two explicit obstructions to reducing the second buyer (Section 'Open questions')

coordinate_compression.claim: With the other three marginal laws fixed, replacing the second buyer value by its mean can raise the optimal posted-price welfare ratio, here from 67/70 to 1.
coordinate_compression.model: Two units, buyer vector (B1,B2) with B1>=B2, seller vector (S1,S2) with S1<=S2, vectors independent, inclusive trade rule S_i<=z<=B_i.

value_convexity.claim: The jointly optimized first-unit value V_lambda is not convex in the law of the second buyer body: V(mix) - (V(delta_1)+V(delta_2))/2 >= lambda/10 for every lambda >= 25/72.
value_convexity.model: Normalized limiting problem with common escaping buyer tails of first moment one; bodies 1<=Z2<=Z1<=2; S2 = 0 w.p. 1/10 and 2 w.p. 9/10; 0<=S1<=S2; kernel g_p(s,z) = 1{s<p} (1 + (z-s) 1{p<=z}); gain cap E g_p(S1,Z1) + E g_p(S2,Z2) <= 2 at every body price p; G = 2 + sum_q E(Z_q-S_q)_+, M = E(S1+S2); V_lambda(mu) = sup { G - lambda M } over first-unit laws, with Z2 ~ mu.
